name: Figmaboy v0.5.5
body:
Figmaboy 0.5.5 rebuilds `/evolve` around first-principles reconstruction. The selected frame remains frozen while a new design emerges inside an empty sibling frame.

Every proposal is rendered in an isolated canvas and sent through visual review with the exact image and deterministic audit before comparison or commit. Designers can inspect screenshots, search Phosphor icons and reusable assets, check fonts, and audit layout and accessibility.

Built-in Codex chat history stays inside Figmaboy. The bundled canvas tools are trusted in-app, so design reads and edits no longer open permission prompts while external filesystem, shell, and network protections remain intact.

Download the installer for your platform below. This release also includes standalone `figmaboy-mcp` binaries and a `SHA256SUMS` file.

macOS builds are ad-hoc signed and are not notarized yet, so first launch may require approval in Privacy & Security. Windows builds are not code-signed yet and may show a SmartScreen warning.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/0xmiki/figmaboy/compare/v0.5.4...v0.5.5

name: Figmaboy v0.5.3
body:
Figmaboy 0.5.3 rebuilds `/evolve` around first-principles reconstruction. The selected frame remains untouched as a frozen reference while Figmaboy creates an empty sibling and constructs the new direction layer by layer. Each pass handles one focused visual objective, with a fixed operation budget that keeps progress visible on the canvas.

The evolve runtime now uses one sequential designer in short-lived `codex exec` workers. Figmaboy validates every proposal before rendering, returns exact errors for bounded corrections, and cleans up worker process trees after each pass. Empty or invalid proposals can no longer create endless retry loops.

The editor also follows new evolution activity automatically, preserves selected parent frames when opening context menus over their children, and separates nested text selection from text editing.

name: Figmaboy v0.5.2
body:
Figmaboy 0.5.2 turns `/evolve` into a parallel design search. Each generation gives three isolated designers different mandates, renders their proposals in separate candidate documents, compares the results visually, and applies the strongest one to the live canvas. The sidebar preserves a compact generation journal after the run.

Large documents now use indexed geometry for culling, snapping, marquee selection, and drop targeting. Normal drags move through a temporary interaction layer and commit once on release. Directional retention and bounded frame previews keep nearby content visible without leaving every SVG layer mounted.

Evolve specialists now start with only the tools they need, clean up their ephemeral threads, and stop on shared system errors instead of repeating an impossible correction loop.

name: Figmaboy v0.5.1
body:
Figmaboy 0.5.1 makes `/evolve` proposals far more reliable. Designer agents fetch the complete native type contract through one read-only tool, and Figmaboy returns exact parser or canvas errors to the same designer for correction.

Large canvases now retain the previous render window until layers in the destination viewport mount. This prevents blank regions during fast panning and scrolling without disabling canvas culling.

name: Figmaboy v0.5.0
body:
Figmaboy 0.5 adds `/evolve`, a design loop that gives an independent director and designer a selected frame and a visual direction. Accepted candidates appear on the canvas as the loop runs, the sidebar explains each pass, and one undo returns to the starting design.

The Codex composer now supports inline skills, Markdown, pasted or dropped image references, prompt copying, clearer stop and approval controls, and saved `/evolve` conversations. Design and Codex share the right sidebar, so switching between inspection and chat no longer moves the canvas between competing panels.

Frames can open in a focused fullscreen preview from the canvas or Layers menu. Editor navigation now uses a clear Back control, page transitions stay quiet, and fixes cover image pasting in Tauri, text editing stability, page startup, home scrolling, and sidebar resizing.

The built-in Codex tab starts Figmaboy's bundled design tools automatically. It does not ask users to install or register an MCP server. Standalone MCP binaries remain available only for people who intentionally control Figmaboy from another Codex client.

Download the installer for your platform below. This release also includes standalone `figmaboy-mcp` binaries and a `SHA256SUMS` file.

name: Figmaboy v0.4.0
body:
Figmaboy 0.4 replaces the embedded Codex terminal with a native Codex app-server sidebar. Chats persist locally per design page, and the sidebar supports saved threads, streaming replies, tool activity, approvals, image attachments, steering, model controls, and context usage.

MCP setup is simpler. The app can install or repair the bundled Figmaboy MCP, and the documentation now leads with a prompt that lets Codex handle setup for the current platform.

Large documents now render fewer off-screen canvas nodes and virtualize the Layers panel. Sidebar resizing, autosave previews, snapping, and initial editor loading do less work. This release also adds Figma-style nested selection, fixes text editing typography and position changes, and moves the interface to Phosphor icons with shared typography tokens.

name: Figmaboy v0.3.0
body:
Figmaboy 0.3 adds projects for organizing related design files without disrupting existing standalone designs. Create a project from the home toolbar, open it, and create focused design files inside it; projects and standalone designs stay visible together in the local workspace.

This release also fixes a Linux desktop freeze when choosing an image for the canvas. Native file dialogs now run asynchronously instead of blocking the application event loop.

Figmaboy is a local-first desktop interface design tool with a native MCP companion for Codex.
